reviewer.independenceStatement: Fresh independent semantic reviewer; did not author or repair the candidate and did not inspect V0, observations, holdouts, other forward outputs, or prior reviews.

gates.name: Coverage
evidence: directing-brief.json: accountContext, singlePlan.audience, demandEvidence, primaryJob/guardrailJob, contracts, contentMechanism, evidencePlan, beats, shots, packaging, experiment, production, assets/carrierEvidence/safety.
brief.md: 发布后复盘 supplies the review sequence and separately requires checking execution compliance and directional support.
Unknown price, compatibility, analytics fields, and actual device/tool are explicit in unknowns with owners and resolution paths.

gates.name: Evidence fidelity
evidence: Claims are classified as user_claim, unknown, or system_inference; no claim is promoted to verified_observation.
claim_demand confines the four question classes to topic clues and expressly rejects population, search-volume, priority, and conversion inferences.

claim_import_scope and claim_final_object limit the proof to one file/one project/one version and one result object; they reject universal compatibility, automation, performance, and causal attribution.
Price and compatibility remain unknown unless current official evidence is captured on recording day.

gates.name: Promise closure
evidence: The title promises four pre-use checks; the cover lists price/system/material/cover; the opening discloses Flova plus human checking within 4 seconds and maps all four items by 12 seconds.
beats verify/import/cover repay each promised item with an operation and explicit proof boundary.
beat_close and contracts.promiseClosure close all four statuses without asserting free use, universal compatibility, automation, or traffic outcomes.
The save CTA is tied to the delivered checklist, and the follow contract names future real-world tests, failure boundaries, and manual corrections.

gates.name: Executability
evidence: Six timed beats and six linked shots specify speech, screen text, image content, function, evidence responsibility, assets, transitions, and edit decisions for a 76-second cut.
Production assigns verification, capture, narration, edit, and publication review to the creator and gives a 255-minute schedule.
Fallbacks cover absent official facts and failed import capture; packaging, CTA, comment coding, metrics, windows, and review order specify publishing and measurement actions.

gates.name: Production feasibility
evidence: The supplied existing screen recording, final vertical clip, and .md file are mapped to shots; only official-page, import, cover, and voice captures must be added.
One creator, desk/screen locations, common recording/editing/browser tools, a 255-minute allocation, and a 70-82-second duration fit the one-person half-day constraint.
Unknown device/tool details have a pre-shoot owner and resolution, and unavailable facts/import success have content fallbacks.

gates.name: Original transfer
evidence: The original task supplies no reference creator or source work, so transfer is explicitly not applicable rather than fabricated.
The plan uses the creator's own project, workflow file, recording, and result and explicitly rejects copied wording, identity symbols, case ownership, and third-party comment identities.

gates.name: Measurement
evidence: singlePlan.experiment declares exactly one primary variable, opening, and locks audience, body order, proof objects, title/cover system, CTA, duration, and publishing conditions.
The main save-rate metric matches the search/save job; 12-second retention and tool-misattribution comments guard comprehension and trust.
The plan includes 24-hour/7-day windows, a four-post A/B minimum, proxy definitions, non-random confounds, and an explicit retain/undecided/stop-change rule.
nonblockingRisks: The B-opening description should explicitly retain Flova disclosure within the first 12 seconds and state its target duration; otherwise a later operator could accidentally vary disclosure amount and duration in addition to opening structure.

gates.name: Safety and rights
evidence: The plan protects comment privacy, rejects prohibited free/universal/automatic/traffic claims, scopes official facts to recording-day evidence, and conditionally requires commercial disclosure.
carrierEvidence.referent_flova_ui acknowledges that the product interface and marks belong to their respective rights holder, but only says to review display rules before publication.
carrierEvidence.referent_final_clip says to confirm that the result contains no unauthorized third-party content, while assets still label the clip and recordings owned.
failures: Authorization for publishing the Flova interface/marks is not established, and the plan does not explicitly block those shots or provide a safe substitute if the display review is unresolved or adverse. Under G7, missing authorization must block asset use or trigger a safe fallback.

The final clip's embedded third-party-content check is pending, but the plan gives no explicit remove/replace/block fallback if that audit finds unlicensed footage, music, fonts, likenesses, or other material.

blocking.issue: Publication rights for product UI/marks and any embedded third-party elements in the final clip are not closed by authorization or an enforceable no-use fallback.
blocking.requiredRevision: For each affected asset, record the verification owner and pre-publication deadline, then state: if public-display rights or applicable display terms cannot be confirmed, the asset is prohibited from the cut and must be replaced with a creator-made schematic, rights-cleared crop/mockup, or other non-infringing carrier. If the final-clip audit finds any unlicensed component, remove or replace it and re-audit before use.

nonblocking.recommendedRevision: Define B's exact duration and explicitly preserve Flova dependency disclosure by 12 seconds so the tested change remains the opening structure rather than disclosure compliance.

requiredRevisions: Close G7 by making unresolved/adverse product-UI display rights an explicit no-use condition with a rights-safe substitute.
Close G7 by adding an explicit remove/replace/block rule for unauthorized third-party components found inside the final clip.

humanApproval.note: Human approval remains separate from reviewer readiness and cannot override failed G7.
